tools.name: resolve_shift_windows_for_thing
tools.title: Resolve shift windows for thing
tools.whenToUse: Use whenever the user's question involves shift-relative time for a specific Thing — current shift, last shift, previous shift, a named shift (shift A, night shift), or any comparison across shifts. Call this tool BEFORE constructing any time range from shift language; never derive shift boundaries yourself. thingName must be an exact Thing name — resolve colloquial equipment names to the canonical Thing first. Vocabulary: "last shift", "previous shift", and "last completed shift" all refer to the lastCompletedShift field; "the shift before that" is recentShifts[1]; "same shift yesterday" is the recentShifts entry with the same name and the prior productionDate. Timezone discipline: the shift pattern runs in the Thing's site timezone (UTC offset siteUtcOffset, read from the Thing), which may differ from the user's timezone — interpret all shift words in site time, and resolve day words inside shift phrases ("yesterday's night shift") against productionDate, which is a site-local date. startTime and endTime are UTC — pass them verbatim as query-window arguments to ThingWorx data services; never pass site-local timestamps to queries. When presenting times to the user, use startTimeLocal and endTimeLocal and label them as site time (they carry the siteUtcOffset suffix); do not convert them into the user's own timezone unless the user explicitly asks. Omit referenceTime unless the user anchors to a specific past instant; referenceTime is UTC. Do not use for absolute time ranges or purely calendar-relative ranges (yesterday, last week) that contain no shift wording.
tools.purpose: Resolve deterministic site-local shift windows for one canonical Thing.
